ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The external view and schematic diagram of a certain model of household spray bottle show that the cross-sectional area of the inner wall of the air cylinder in the bottle is $S=3.0{\times}10^{-4}m^{2}$, the maximum stroke of the piston is $l{=}1.6\times10^{-1}\mathrm{m}$, and the gas inside the bottle needs to reach a pressure of $p=1.3\times 10^{5}\mathrm{Pa}$ or higher for normal spraying. After filling the bottle with water, the piston connected to the handle is pressed to the bottom of the air cylinder, at which point the volume of the gas inside the bottle is $1.2\times10^{-3}\mathrm{m^3}$, the pressure is $p_{1}=1.0\times10^{5}$ Pa, and the temperature is $27^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$. The atmospheric pressure is known to be $p_{0}{=}1.0{\times}10^{5}\mathrm{Pa}$.

1. Place the watering can outdoors where the outdoor temperature is $9^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$. What is the pressure of the gas inside the can after it stabilizes?
2. In an outdoor environment with a constant temperature, how many times must the handle be pumped to pressurize the spray bottle to reach its working state?

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the picture shows a household pump spray bottle; the schematic on the right shows a handle-driven piston/air cylinder at the top, a spray/press handle, and a catheter extending down into the liquid, so pumping the handle injects air into the fixed gas space above the water. Then reason as follows. From the text take the initial gas volume V=1.2×10^-3 m^3, initial pressure p1=1.0×10^5 Pa, initial temperature 27°C=300 K, outdoor temperature 9°C=282 K, air-cylinder area S=3.0×10^-4 m^2, stroke l=1.6×10^-1 m, atmospheric pressure p0=1.0×10^5 Pa, and working pressure p=1.3×10^5 Pa. For part 1, because the gas amount and bottle volume are unchanged after moving outdoors, use p/T=constant: p_out=p1 T_out/T_in=1.0×10^5×282/300≈0.94×10^5 Pa. For part 2, each full pump stroke draws in and injects atmospheric air of volume ΔV=Sl=4.8×10^-5 m^3. At fixed outdoor temperature and fixed bottle gas volume, each stroke raises the bottle pressure by Δp=p0ΔV/V. Therefore solve N≥(1.3×10^5−0.94×10^5)/(p0Sl/V), giving N=9 pumps.

图像描述：左侧是一个家用喷壶的外观图，瓶身为橙色，上部有黑色喷头、喷嘴和侧面的按压手柄；右侧是结构示意图，标出了 Handle、Press handle 和 Catheter，顶部有由手柄带动的活塞/气筒结构，导管向下伸入瓶内液体中，瓶中虚线表示液体区域，液面上方为空气空间。因此按动手柄会把外界空气经气筒压入瓶内水面上方的固定气体空间。

推理：已知瓶内气体初态体积 V=1.2×10^-3 m^3，压强 p1=1.0×10^5 Pa，温度 27℃=300 K；室外温度 9℃=282 K。移到室外稳定后，瓶内气体物质的量和体积不变，所以 p/T 恒定：p_out=p1·T_out/T_in=1.0×10^5×282/300=9.4×10^4 Pa=0.94×10^5 Pa。

室外恒温下打气，每次满行程吸入并压入的外界空气体积为 ΔV=Sl=(3.0×10^-4)(1.6×10^-1)=4.8×10^-5 m^3。瓶内气体体积不变且温度不变，每次增加的压强为 Δp=p0ΔV/V=1.0×10^5×(4.8×10^-5)/(1.2×10^-3)=4.0×10^3 Pa。工作压强需达到 1.3×10^5 Pa，从室外稳定后的 0.94×10^5 Pa 起，需要增加 1.3×10^5-0.94×10^5=3.6×10^4 Pa，所以次数 N=3.6×10^4/(4.0×10^3)=9。

室外恒温打气时，目标工作压强 p=1.3×10^5 Pa。每压一次手柄，气筒吸入并压入瓶内的外界空气体积为 Sl，其中 S=3.0×10^-4 m^2，l=1.6×10^-1 m，所以每次增加的气体物质的量为 n_add=p0Sl/(RT2)。达到工作状态所需总物质的量为 n_req=pV/(RT2)，瓶中原有物质的量为 n1=p1V/(RT1)。因此所需次数 N=ceil((n_req-n1)/n_add)=ceil([pV/(RT2)-p1V/(RT1)]/[p0Sl/(RT2)])。代入得 N=ceil([1.3×10^5×1.2×10^-3-1.0×10^5×1.2×10^-3×282/300]/[1.0×10^5×3.0×10^-4×1.6×10^-1])=ceil(43.2/4.8)=9。

raw_record.original_question:
The external view and schematic diagram of a certain model of household spray bottle show that the cross-sectional area of the inner wall of the air cylinder in the bottle is $S=3.0{\times}10^{-4}m^{2}$, the maximum stroke of the piston is $l{=}1.6\times10^{-1}\mathrm{m}$, and the gas inside the bottle needs to reach a pressure of $p=1.3\times 10^{5}\mathrm{Pa}$ or higher for normal spraying. After filling the bottle with water, the piston connected to the handle is pressed to the bottom of the air cylinder, at which point the volume of the gas inside the bottle is $1.2\times10^{-3}\mathrm{m^3}$, the pressure is $p_{1}=1.0\times10^{5}$ Pa, and the temperature is $27^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$. The atmospheric pressure is known to be $p_{0}{=}1.0{\times}10^{5}\mathrm{Pa}$.

1. Place the watering can outdoors where the outdoor temperature is $9^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$. What is the pressure of the gas inside the can after it stabilizes?
2. In an outdoor environment with a constant temperature, how many times must the handle be pumped to pressurize the spray bottle to reach its working state?
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: On the left is an appearance diagram of a household spray bottle, the bottle body is orange, and the upper part has a black spray head, nozzle, and side press handle; on the right is a structural schematic diagram, marking Handle, Press handle and Catheter, with a piston/air-cylinder structure driven by the handle at the top, and the catheter extends downward into the liquid in the bottle; the dashed lines in the bottle indicate the liquid region, and above the liquid surface is an air space. Therefore pressing the handle will press outside air through the air cylinder into the fixed gas space above the water surface in the bottle.

Reasoning: It is known that the initial-state volume of the gas in the bottle is V=1.2×10^-3 m^3, the pressure p1=1.0×10^5 Pa, and the temperature 27℃=300 K; the outdoor temperature is 9℃=282 K. After being moved outdoors and stabilized, the amount of substance and volume of the gas in the bottle remain unchanged, so p/T is constant: p_out=p1·T_out/T_in=1.0×10^5×282/300=9.4×10^4 Pa=0.94×10^5 Pa.

Pumping air under outdoor constant temperature, the volume of outside air inhaled and pressed in each full stroke is ΔV=Sl=(3.0×10^-4)(1.6×10^-1)=4.8×10^-5 m^3. The volume of the gas in the bottle remains unchanged and the temperature remains unchanged, so the pressure increased each time is Δp=p0ΔV/V=1.0×10^5×(4.8×10^-5)/(1.2×10^-3)=4.0×10^3 Pa. The working pressure needs to reach 1.3×10^5 Pa; starting from 0.94×10^5 Pa after outdoor stabilization, it is necessary to increase by 1.3×10^5-0.94×10^5=3.6×10^4 Pa, so the number of times N=3.6×10^4/(4.0×10^3)=9.
